name: DeepProtein benchmark
description: Benchmark of sequence-based, graph-based and pretrained protein models, plus two chemistry LLMs, over protein function, localization, interaction, epitope and paratope, developability, CRISPR repair and structure prediction tasks, with datasets taken from TAPE, PEER and TDC.

attributes.task: Protein sequence learning across nine task groups
attributes.scope_note: Each task keeps the split of its original benchmark; every method is trained with five random seeds and the mean and standard deviation are reported.
attributes.source_locator: Results, 'Each individual split is reported from Tables 2-7'; Tables 2 to 8
limitations: Author-reported: the DeepProtein authors both run the baselines and introduce DeepProt-T5.
Residue-level and secondary structure tasks were not run for structure-based and language models (Table 7 footnote).

name: DeepProtein: deep learning library and benchmark for protein sequence learning
description: Primary source retrieved and hashed for the 2026-10-11 protein and structure literature pass.

attributes.version: Version of record, Bioinformatics 2025 (PMC12553333 JATS full text)
limitations: Tables 2 to 8. Table 1 (a feature comparison with earlier benchmark libraries), Table 9 (default hyperparameters) and the task-instruction table hold no measurements and were not extracted.

The regression correlation columns are printed as rho. The Evaluation metrics section defines rho as Spearman rank correlation; Figure 3's caption calls it 'Spearman (Pearson) Coefficient'. The section's definition is used.

Cells printed as '/' are not measurements: the Table 7 footnote says structure-based and pretrained protein language models were disregarded for residue-level and secondary structure prediction. They are left out, not recorded as zero.
Bold, underline and the '**' significance marks are kept in printed_value where they are part of the printed cell; the article's own statistical tests were not re-run.

evidence_concerns.message: Figure 3's caption calls the regression metric 'Spearman (Pearson) Coefficient' while the Evaluation metrics section defines rho as Spearman rank correlation and R2 separately. The section's definition is taken as authoritative and the rho columns are recorded as Spearman; the caption wording is noted so a reader of the figure is not surprised.
evidence_concerns.source_locator: Tables 2, 4 and 6 column headings 'rho' and 'R2'; Figure 3 caption

name: Relevance of DeepProtein Stability (rho) to "Assess methods for protein stability experiments"
description: Correlation of predicted with measured stability on the TAPE stability split, for protein language models and conventional sequence and graph baselines.

attributes.endpoint: Rank correlation between predicted and measured stability on the TAPE stability test split (53571/2512/12851 train/valid/test), mean over five seeds
attributes.rationale: Proxy, not direct: the use case needs per-method correlation and error on held-out or dissimilar proteins with a stated construct and endpoint, and this protocol gives correlation on one supervised split of designed mini-protein stability measurements. It says nothing about antisymmetry on reverse variants, about transfer to larger proteins, or about ddG in kcal/mol.
constraints: Supervised split: every model is trained on the task's training set, so these values are not comparable with zero-shot stability rankings.
Spearman rank correlation on one supervised split; not comparable with zero-shot stability rankings or with ddG values in kcal/mol.
Compare only within this protocol and this split.
Inspect every linked evaluation's source locator before citing a result.
limitations: Author-reported: the DeepProtein authors ran every baseline and also introduce DeepProt-T5, which tops several tasks.
Graphormer ran out of memory on this task, so its cell is recorded with a missing value reason rather than a score.
One dataset and one split; no held-out-protein or homology-split stability evaluation.

The TAPE stability truth set is proteolysis-derived stability of designed mini-proteins, so it is biased towards small designed domains and away from the larger natural proteins the use case asks about.
attributes.reason: Not shown: the source carries an evidence concern noting that Figure 3's caption calls the regression metric 'Spearman (Pearson) Coefficient' while the Evaluation metrics section defines it as Spearman. A source with evidence concerns withholds every judgement that cites it, so this judgement and the use-case summary edit that would describe it are held until the concern is cleared.
